findings.reason: the plan should state that the door resolves the run's home from the ambient `crew_home()` (the same home the record was read from), which keeps the change inside `reckon/_store.py`, `reckon/crew/process_signal.py`, `reckon/crew/recovery_liveness.py` and the test, and drops the unsupportable "a caller with a stale or isolated ambient `RECKON_HOME` still matches the run's own worker" claim for that door.
findings.text: the deliverable says each door passes "the home of the run it holds: `_env_scan_run_pid` the home its record was read from", but `local_liveness(record)` and `_env_scan_run_pid(record)` receive only a record and no home, and a live pointer carries no home field; `local_liveness` has five call sites (`sprint_liveness.py:153`, `resumption.py:1012`, `recovery_watch.py:1059`, `recovery_classification.py:209`, `runs.py:1624`), none of which names a home, so "the home its record was read from" is the ambient `crew_home()` and nowhere else — a literal reading sends the implementer to plumb a home through five files that are not in the declared write paths

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — every cited symbol resolves at the named module (`_processes_owning_run` `process_signal.py:148`; `local_liveness` `recovery_liveness.py:1001`; `_env_scan_run_pid` `:1091`; `_config_home` `_store.py:128`; `crew_home` `run_paths.py:19`; `run_dir` `runs.py:81`), the cited test id and its `[codex]` parametrization exist, the evidence run and job `1287701` resolve, and `a-run-has-one-live-writer` §2 exists.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — §1's done-when (`docs/plans/a-run-mark-is-read-in-its-own-crew-home.html:34`) is measurable (a named new test asserting one child named, `local_liveness` not-alive, the no-`RECKON_HOME` case both ways, and slash/symlink equivalence) and declares a negative control that flips the asserted outcome — removing the crew-home comparison makes `_processes_owning_run` name both children, so the "only the first child" assertion fails.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the only evidence location named is "the run directory", a durable path under the crew home, and the run's own record (`~/.config/reckon/crew/runs/r-20261016T212841719818-…/`) confirms run directories are where a node's gate logs live; nothing points at a scratchpad or node-local `/tmp`.
rubric_items.naming: pass — no plan label, stage name, ticket number or version tag reaches code; the proposed test filename reads as a mechanism sentence without the plan, and the plan's own `a-run-has-one-live-writer §2` reference lives in plan prose, which the tracker owns.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — the root cause matches the evidence and the mechanism produces the measure, but the deliverable's home-provenance claim is not implementable as written at the `local_liveness` door.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — one deliverable (narrow the one matcher to the run's crew home); the four write paths, the ruff floor and the merge-time population run are conditions on that deliverable, not a second one.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — the plan declares `plan-standalone` with a reason ("no live plan waits on it, and it waits on none"), the one plan it references (`a-run-has-one-live-writer`) is `plan-status: done` and carries the cited §2 ("A worker never outlives its supervisor"), and no other plan under `docs/plans/` names this slug, so no dependency edge is owed or missing.
